title: Olympos, Çıralı & Yanartaş Eternal Flames: Quiet Coastal Stay
seoTitle: Çıralı & Olympos Guide: Yanartaş Flames & Sea Turtles
metaDescription: Compare Çıralı and Olympos, time your Yanartaş eternal flames hike, follow Caretta caretta turtle rules, and pair Phaselis with Tahtalı cable car.
quickAnswer: Çıralı and Olympos share a single 3.2-kilometer pebble-and-sand bay inside Olympos-Beydağları Coastal National Park, yet feel worlds apart: Çıralı offers quiet orchard bungalows right behind the sea, while Olympos centers on forested ruins and backpacker treehouses. Hike up to Yanartaş at dusk, respect Caretta caretta turtle protections, and pair the stay with Phaselis and Tahtalı cable car.

body.text: What is the difference between Çıralı and Olympos?

Çıralı occupies the wide northern and central stretch of the bay with low-rise family bungalows, citrus gardens, and direct beach access suited to couples and families seeking silence. Olympos sits tucked inside a narrow wooded valley at the southern end, known for rustic wooden cabins, rock-climbing groups, and the forested archaeological ruins you walk through to reach the water.

A short beach walk links both villages, whereas driving requires a 35-minute detour via the D400. Per the [Ministry of Culture and Tourism](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=OLY01&DistId=OLY), Olympos also forms a 7.5-kilometer segment of the [Lycian Way](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/lycian-way-turkey).

body.text: When is the best time to hike up to Yanartaş (Chimaera)?

Start the uphill stone-step climb to Yanartaş (Chimaera) 45 to 60 minutes before sunset so you hike the rocky 1-kilometer trail in daylight and watch the natural methane flames glow brightly as twilight settles. Arriving at midday makes the flames pale and hard to spot under harsh sun, while hiking up after dark increases the risk of rolled ankles.

As [2026 Yanartaş visitor guidance](https://viatravelers.com/flaming-rocks-in-turkey/) confirms, the flame field sits roughly 1 kilometer inland from Çıralı Beach at around 250 meters elevation inside Olympos-Beydağları Coastal National Park—and despite frequent confusion online, there is no cable car to Yanartaş. The climb takes 20 to 35 minutes on uneven ancient paving stones. Pack a headlamp (red-light mode is best), closed-toe sneakers or trail shoes, and drinking water; skip plastic flip-flops on the descent.
Why is Çıralı protected for Caretta caretta sea turtles?

Çıralı Beach is one of the Mediterranean's most important remaining nesting grounds for the endangered loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta). Because female turtles lay eggs in the sand at night from May through August and hatchlings orient toward natural moonlight on the sea, strict national-park rules limit coastal building heights, beach lighting, and night-time shore access.

Conservation monitoring led locally alongside [WWF](https://wwf.panda.org/wwf_news/?15130/Sea-and-snow-on-Turkeys-Mediterranean-coast) and [WWF-Türkiye](https://www.wwf.org.tr/kesfet/biyocesitlilik/turler/deniz_kaplumbagalari/) explains why Çıralı never turned into a concrete resort strip like parts of Kemer or Antalya. During nesting and hatching months (May through September/October), [local nesting-zone guidelines](https://escape2olympos.com/2026/06/07/cirali-caretta-caretta-nesting-area-loggerhead-turtle-guide/) require visitors to follow simple habits:

items: Respect wire nest cages: Never step near, lean on, or plant beach umbrellas beside marked nesting enclosures.
Keep the beach dark after sunset: Avoid flash photography, phone torches, and beach bonfires that disorient hatchlings away from the water.
Leave no gear behind: Clear towels, chairs, and litter before dusk so nesting females have an unobstructed path up the sand.

How do you pair it with Phaselis and Tahtalı cable car?

Pair Çıralı with Phaselis Ancient City and the Olympos Teleferik (Tahtalı cable car) in one north-bound D400 loop, both 25–35 minutes away. Ride the cable car first thing before midday clouds wrap the summit, then drop down to Phaselis for pine-shaded ruins and an afternoon swim.

According to [Olympos Teleferik](https://www.olymposteleferik.com/en/index.html), the cable car lifts visitors from the coastal national park to the 2,365-meter summit of Tahtalı Mountain—carry a light fleece even in June or September, as summit air runs 15°C cooler than the coast. Afterward, drive 15 minutes to [Phaselis Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=PHS01&DistId=PHS), founded in 690 BC by Rhodian colonists around three sheltered natural harbors and visited by Roman Emperor Hadrian in AD 129. Walk the colonnaded main street, swim in the calm South Harbor, and return to Çıralı in time for a dusk climb to Yanartaş.

faq.q: How far is Çıralı from Antalya Airport?
faq.a: Çıralı lies roughly 95 kilometers southwest of Antalya Airport (AYT), about a 1 hour 30 minute to 1 hour 45 minute drive along the D400 highway via Kemer, followed by a winding 7-kilometer descent into the valley.

faq.q: Can you walk between Çıralı and Olympos Ancient City?
faq.a: Yes. Walk south along Çıralı Beach for 10 to 15 minutes to reach the beachside ticket gate of Olympos Ancient City. Carry your Museum Pass Türkiye or payment card for entry.

faq.q: Is the Olympos Teleferik cable car located inside Olympos village?
faq.a: No. Despite its name, the Olympos Teleferik lower station sits north of Çıralı off the Tekirova–Kemer highway, roughly 25–30 minutes by car from Çıralı and 40 minutes from Olympos village.

faq.q: Are you guaranteed to see Caretta caretta sea turtles in Çıralı?
faq.a: No, and ethical guides never promise sightings. Nesting happens quietly at night when the beach is restricted, while hatchling emergences occur unpredictably at dawn or night in late July through September.

faq.q: Do I need a rental car to stay in Çıralı?
faq.a: Not if you only want to swim, bike to Yanartaş, and walk to Olympos ruins. However, a rental car or pre-booked private driver makes pairing Phaselis, Tahtalı cable car, and Ulupınar creek restaurants much easier.

faq.q: How many nights should I spend in Çıralı?
faq.a: Two to three nights fit cleanly: one day for Olympos ruins, beach time, and dusk at Yanartaş; one day for Tahtalı cable car and Phaselis; and an optional third day for an Adrasan–Suluada or coastal boat trip.
